## DL-271 — Onboarding credential, recovery and pairing feedback

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-271
unit_type: decision_record
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: 'DL-271 records the PM7 final onboarding batch accepted through the lead on 2026-10-31. DL-271 FO-11,
  2026-10-31: where an OpenCode server requires its own HTTP Basic credentials, the Password field asks for that server’s
  password, not an AI provider’s API key or the person’s Puppet Master sign-in. Its hint states that distinction and
  identifies credential custody in the OS keychain on the selected execution host, through the existing credential owner.
  Optional server auth stays optional when the server needs none. Protected entry, secret-free readback and exact host/account
  binding remain; an API-key-only hint is used only on an actual API-key field. DL-271 FO-12, 2026-10-31: Protect’s missing-access
  guidance is count-neutral: ask for the access details without claiming a fixed number of fields. The selected Backup
  destination family, auth method and credential mode determine the actual required fields and validation through their
  existing owner. Changing the line never omits a required credential, locator, region or temporary-session value and
  never turns incomplete access into an available Connect action. DL-271 Unlock wording, 2026-10-31: ask for your recovery
  phrase, rather than six words or another fixed word count. The Recovery Kit is not a six-word format (PWIZ-025/BRS-018);
  the Backup owner still defines and verifies the real protected recovery material and its exact source/target binding.
  The wording admits no new phrase format, key derivation, unlock proof or weaker secret-handling rule. DL-271 weak-key
  eligibility, 2026-10-31: Choose a key may list a DSA or RSA-1024 key as Too weak to use, but it cannot be selected,
  used as a default, advanced or installed. The refusal reads Older key type — too weak to use. Check this eligibility
  before an existing authorization, matching prior profile or passphrase/unlock state; those cannot make a weak key usable.
  A retained weak selection must be replaced by an owner-eligible key before the flow advances. Other keys keep their
  existing owner checks, identity binding and custody; the shared list never exposes or moves a private half. DL-271
  initial request waiting, 2026-10-31: while the current invitation is live and no device request has arrived, Your Server
  is ready shows No requests yet with Check again. Checking re-reads the current owner run; a real arriving request also
  updates that view. This neutral state is not an error and invents no candidate, approval or trust. Continue retains
  its existing Server-ready gates. Keep it distinct from DL-259 FO-7’s answered approval/rejection: a completed request
  stays answered, and a fresh request requires the existing new-code/new-generation route. DL-271 FO-14, 2026-10-31:
  long tokens in an opened question note wrap within its available width, so their full text is readable without horizontal
  scrolling. Keep vertical scrolling when the note exceeds its available height. This applies to Plain English and Expert,
  including NieR, and visual wrapping preserves the exact token for copying; it adds no second note renderer or per-family

### DL-273 — Retire unselected hosted offerings; keep self-managed services and defer restricted tokens

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-273

  represented only by forgejo_self_managed. A hosting provider whose terms forbid AI-generated Projects is not useful
  to Puppet Master, because Puppet Master’s Projects are AI-written; such a host is ineligible. The earlier hosted variant
  entered the source proposal in commit 3e1842da40 on 2026-09-02, not through a Jared ruling. Current instance, adapter,
  onboarding and embedded storage profiles admit only the own-server Forgejo variant and require the real address and
  normal owner verification, with no implicit account or repository authority. Gitea is self-managed only under this
  same decision. On repository-restricted Forgejo tokens Jared said "we can leave it for now." That question remains
  open and deliberately deferred; the existing account-based flow stays unchanged and no support is admitted or permanently
  rejected. This closes DL-272’s hosted-provider admission question and records the restricted-token deferral as decided.

### DL-281 - One Settings Ladder And The Word Computer

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-281
unit_type: decision_record
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: |-
  S1–S3 are accepted. Jared's clarification, 2026-11-02, was: "To clarify, when I say separate settings for different environments, that is what T3
  calls the different computers, but it is where Puppet Master runs its work. I am not sure what we call it." The approved on-screen word is Computer, each by its own name, with This computer for the current one. It means the Server doing the work and the Host where programs, paths or hardware matter; Device means the screen in front of the person. Execution Environment is a finer resource identity, never another settings level.

  Ordinary values follow Default, Everywhere, the offered Computer or Device level, Project when present, then existing owner/chat/run/tab levels. Managed remains above them. Most shared rows may differ per Computer and Project; screen, Project-file, same-for-you and owner-thing rows keep their declared exceptions. Project normally wins; declared safety answers combine more carefully and Computer capacity is a ceiling. Unknown/custom protective combinations use the owner's declared fallback, not an invented ordering. SSYS-002/059 owns classification and resolution. This supersedes the universal Project-only persistence and inheritance bans, resolves q-035 in favor of a real ordinary Everywhere store, and leaves source-memory ledgers unchanged.

### DL-282 - One Settings Home And Explicit Joining

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-282
unit_type: decision_record
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: |-
  S7 and S12 are accepted. One Computer keeps the shared settings and other same-owner Computers follow it through explicit protected trust. Each level has one writer and bounded read-only mirrors or caches. A Computer that cannot reach the writer may show the last known values with their age; it cannot queue edits, elect itself writer or silently fail over. Joining two existing setups first chooses the home and shows exact differences, alternatives and affected contexts. The accepted join Undo lasts 30 days. Ordinary per-setting Undo keeps its existing owner policy.

  Home transfer verifies the copy and history, fences the old writer and switches the role generation once. A stale copy acknowledgement cannot prove the old writer is fenced; recovery without that proof remains blocked. Settings following never grants access to Projects, files, chats or another person's work. SSYS-060 and SRV-016 own these rules, with storage binding them rather than creating another synchronization engine.

### DL-291 - Two Equal Ways To Join A Project With Report And Undo

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-291
unit_type: decision_record
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: |-
  N2, N9, N11, N13, N20, N25 and N27 and Q1/Q2 are accepted. Make a project from this chat and Move this chat into a project are equal first-class choices, neither preselected. Each names what will happen, shows a fresh preview, acts through a button naming the action, then reports moved/stayed/held/failed work and offers Undo. Moving into an existing Project defaults to a separate branch/worktree or admitted Jujutsu change/bookmark and a chosen folder; direct main is Advanced. Keep-both is the conflict default; unsaved work is never overwritten.

  A new Project is committed/listed first. Files copy and verify before the single live writer cuts over, including across Computers. The retained thread ID gets full destination-owned history; original immutable events, usage and receipts stay sealed with lineage and no re-charge. Goal, Crew and Plan default to linked new destination records; only a complete separate owner rebind may change association. Active work is stopped/fenced and exact future schedules are held and explicitly re-admitted with fresh target authority, never silently retargeted or dispatched twice.

  Undo ends at first new work or seven days. It never deletes remote repositories, branches, backups, changed work or independently retained canonical/audit custody. Regular applies by the person; N27 admits the guarded YOLO owner route only when the task clearly asks for a new Project or names the existing destination. Ambiguous convert this still asks for a destination. Merge means a chat joining a Project, not two chats; moving Project chats between Projects comes later.

### DL-297 - Inspect Sources Keep Format In Settings And Protect Backups

New Project inspects every admitted local/Server/SSH/SMB/NFS/mounted source read-only, reporting actual Git/Jujutsu history, branch/bookmark, dirty state, remotes, submodules, LFS, hooks and duplicate-copy evidence. Archive pauses its schedule and preserves the last good backup, with no prune; unarchive restores eligibility, not a hidden run or cleared Stop. Recovery Kit remains protected. Restore rewrites PM-internal identities while external forge identity remains historical until revalidated.

### DL-299 - Approve A Build Grant Once And Show Every Target

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-299

status: accepted

  Jared asked: "Isnt orchestrator going to need a lot of permissions to fully build an entire platform from plans that the planning wizard makes? Its hands off from the human in that process so I would think so." O1–O3 are accepted as recommended. The person approves one exact Plan-bound build grant listing needed operations and resources: repository create/push, publication namespaces, CI setup/execution and deployment targets. The Orchestrator and narrower children then run YOLO within that grant, without repeating those ordinary prompts. A changed Plan, target, permission ceiling or Stop/revocation generation never silently widens it; no agent issues, expands or renews its own grant.

  A verified created-resource manifest binds stable IDs/generations and ownership receipts. The build may change or clean up what this grant demonstrably created, within the enumerated operations. Naming a pre-existing resource does not grant deletion, a name prefix is not ownership and a namespace does not authorize every child object. This is the narrow grant exception to Y1's ordinary risky-action asks, never permission to force-push main, touch unrelated resources or bypass FileSafe/trust/secrets. Secrets, paid sign-ups and protected administration retain their separate human choices.

  What the build did reads the existing work/History projection and lists each remote action, exact target, authority and outcome, including pending, blocked or unknown. One run-owner Stop fences new dispatch and children. Undo is offered only where safe; otherwise say No safe Undo. Existing final YOLO checks remain. App Goals/Crew and cross-project requests cannot borrow this Project's grant.

### DL-340 - The June Legacy Rule Reads Four Older Words As Passed

Jared approved stream C's question Q-A on 2026-11-05 ("i approve all of it", option 1): in the 55 June audit directories only, the compatibility inference reads four older words as passed. This record lists the words, the limit and the counts.

In the 55 June directories of the legacy format rule (PLS-026), when the run requests no companion file (closure matrix, audit report, effective status, scope manifest or impact matrix) as a source and reads no input through a symlink, and only for a frozen file other than the closure matrix, whose frozen part is only a prefix, the compatibility inference of scripts/pm-audit-closure.py reads four older words as passed: the claim statuses pass, supported_by_source_atoms and previously_closed, and a validator result with status expected_fail whose command is one of five governance commands (pm-plans-verify.py run-gates, verify-spec-lock, validate-evidence and validate-plan-graph, and pm-shard-plans.py --check). Those five failed in June only on stale generated files, which a governance seal refreshes. Every other field of such a row keeps its meaning (an issue list, an overclaim list or a failing status still makes the row actionable), and any other expected_fail result stays actionable. Directories from July 2026 on, files added after the freeze, and edited or symlinked files get the full rules.

The registry report keeps its status, row count, error count and error kinds; only the current digests in 142 pre-existing stale-hash diagnostics change, because this branch edits files they hash.

### DL-341 - Command Definitions Record Judgments, And UCC-230 Gains Nullable Fields, Canon Enum Spelling, Identity Aliases And The Chat-Tool Approval Branch

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-341
unit_type: decision
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: >-
  DL-341 amends the pm.command_payload_definitions.v1 format and the UCC-230 map in Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md
  after rounds 1 to 3 of the blind review of the 275 Q5 command payload definitions (DL-333). In round 1 all five
  review slices failed (3 blockers, 27 majors, 42 minors) while scripts/pm-command-payload-defs-check.py passed.
  Part of the cause was the format and the map: writers had nowhere to record a judgment except a YAML comment,
  which no tool reads, the vocabulary had no nullable form and forced snake_case enum values, and the map missed
  aliases and rules that canon states. Format: a definition records each judgment it makes in an optional judgments
  list of key, choice and gap_note entries. The key is command_kind, response_kind, disabled_reason_codes,
  error_codes, owner_request, owner_result, aliases, omitted:<field> for a field it deliberately leaves out, or
  field:<arg path>; the choice is what the definition chose, equal to its own value for a fixed key; the gap_note
  says what canon lacks or where it disagrees. A judgment carries no provenance, a canon field whose source or
  gap_note says JUDGMENT is a provenance finding, and reviewers check judgments as they check fields. A definitions
  block holds no YAML comment, whatever it says, and no string that names review or evidence material. A field
  marked nullable: true may be JSON null, with any required value, except a required row-group identity or a
  restated common optional field, which keeps its canonical type. Enum values keep canon's exact spelling: non-empty
  strings without surrounding whitespace, unique within the field. Map: cmd.runtime.approve and cmd.runtime.decline
  define both the node approval shape and the HITL-038 chat-tool shape, through conditional identity exemptions that
  require blocked_sequence and allowed_action_id on every approval_kind branch except chat_tool and forbid them on
  chat_tool; canon names only the chat_tool value of approval_kind, so the definition marks that field a gap. Owner
  states maintenance_cutoffs_pending (DL-403, and since the DL-446 and DL-447 cutoffs the hold until their
  approvals pass) and dedup_hold_pending (DL-444, DL-445) map to not_configured. The thirteen CRAU-095 local-runtime
  reason codes and the UCC-111 safe-point retry states safe_point_missing and state_changed map to closed codes;
  canon names those codes without giving them closed codes, so each mapping is a worker's choice under DL-333
  resolution 6 as the stream C lead applies it, and four CRAU-095 mappings are asked of the CRAU owner
  (crau_owner_questions). A definition may tie the owner states it shows to their codes in owner_state_codes. identity_aliases lets gist_id stand for memory_item_id
  (UCC-084..UCC-088) and investigation_id for debug_session_id (UCC-077..UCC-083) without renaming canon. Canon
  already decided three further map corrections, made here with their sources: cmd.terminal.focus_session,
  compose.save_scenario, compose.run_scenario, set_context and set_namespace are recorded aliases with no
  definition; cmd.runtime.locate_and_verify_recovery and cmd.runtime.abandon_recovery are pre-attempt admissible, so
  they never require attempt_id; and worktree_lifecycle_state is required when a command mutates worktree state, as
  the overlay cell says, rather than for every domain action, so cmd.git.worktree.request_prune, which never mutates
  worktree state (GI-041), does not carry it. This entry was amended in place on 2026-11-07, before it reached main,
  after rounds 2 and 3 of the review (round_2_changes, round_3_changes), and on 2026-11-08 after the first,
  second and fifth max reviews (max_review_changes), which add to non_definition_tokens the two assistant worktree
  compatibility aliases CV-160 records, cmd.chat.worktree.create_pr and cmd.chat.worktree.open_files, the two
  worktree compatibility spellings canon targets, cmd.worktree.provision to cmd.git.worktree.create and
  cmd.worktree.release to cmd.git.worktree.release (CS-066, UCC-145), and the safe-point compatibility alias
  cmd.orchestrator.restore_safe_point_then_retry, whose exact contract names the wrapper
  cmd.orchestrator.safe_point_retry as its alias_of_command_id and normalizes it to
  cmd.runtime.restore_safe_point_then_retry (UCC-111). Jared's only words remain "approve all" (DL-333). The coordinator's
  ruling, quoted verbatim in coordinator_resolutions, is the only coordinator resolution in this entry; how it was
  applied, the lead's implementation of resolution 2, the workers' own calls, the application of DL-333 resolution 6
  and the lead's proposals are listed separately and labelled by who made them. This entry changes no owner-doc
  definition; the per-slice fixers bring the definitions to these rules.
coordinator_resolutions:
  - "Ruling (pm-mail 1107140349-9370, pm7-build, 2026-11-07T14:03Z), verbatim: \"All five as you recommend, recorded as coordinator resolutions under DL-333/DL-341. (1) (a): an identity exemption for the HITL-038 chat-tool branch, with both shapes defined; don't leave chat-tool approval without a command. (2) Yes to all three. Add checker rules so every judgment has a key, a choice and a gap_note, and no judgment can claim canon provenance; reviewers check judgments the same way as fields. (3) Yes. (4) Yes: aliases, never renaming canon. (5) Out of this branch, but not dropped: Jared wants everything finalized, so the eight unrouted ids become a follow-up packet (Q5b) in your queue, done before the final reseal.\""

The definition lists them, keeps both fields with required_when on the node branch, and offers the chat_tool branch in a required approval_kind enum, so both the OrchestratorNodeApprovalRequestV1 shape and the RuntimeApproveV3ToolRequest or RuntimeDeclineV3ToolRequest shape are defined. Raised by the stream C lead after the recheck of the Sol 6.1 max fixes."

The recovery_unavailable_resolution_receipt reason_code enum (Plans/storage_value_registry.json) has storage_read_only, storage_io_exhausted, recovery_source_not_verified and explicit_confirmation_required, which are result reasons, not disabled states.   - "Browser control rows' owner request (asked of the Section15_MVP_Promoted_Features_Spec.md owner and the owner of Plans/section15_browser_program_contracts.schema.json): the wiring rows of cmd.browser.share_with_agent, cmd.browser.revoke_share_with_agent, cmd.browser.take_over, cmd.browser.pause_agent, cmd.browser.let_agent_continue and cmd.browser.stop_agent_keep_browser name BrowserActionRequestV2, whose command_id enum lists them, but the request requires a closed browser_action whose action_type enum holds page and tab primitives only: no share, revoke-share, takeover or agent-control action, and no field for share's thread_id or take_over's takeover_choice. The same holds for cmd.browser.detach_browser_tab, cmd.browser.open_devtools, cmd.browser.toggle_devtools_dock, cmd.browser.focus_browser_tab, cmd.browser.promote_to_normal_browsing, cmd.browser.reopen, cmd.browser.retry and cmd.browser.keep_closed, which have no detach, DevTools, dock, session-tab reveal, promotion or session-recovery action and, for open_devtools, toggle_devtools_dock, focus_browser_tab and promote_to_normal_browsing, no field for mode, dock, where, by, background or target_workspace_tab_id. SMPFS-328's definitions keep the wired request, map these fourteen commands onto no action_type, never turn share or revoke into a capture, and have a handler refuse them with handler_unavailable. Should BrowserActionRequestV2 gain session-control actions with those fields, should these commands name a different owner request, or should the two layout-only rows (toggle_devtools_dock, focus_browser_tab) be handled by the shell with no owner request? The request also has no field for the capture rows' optional thread_id, which SMPFS-328 leaves on the UICommand envelope, or for the four screenshot rows' scope (clip or full), which SMPFS-328 keeps as an arg; SMPFS-328 maps the screenshot rows to action_type screenshot and the pick-element and add-selection rows to snapshot, as its own choices. GRS-218 uses each edition's own schema_id for the update and the thread's scope for the start. Raised in the fix round after the fifth Sol 6.1 max review, at the closure lead's request."

### DL-473 - Auto Placement And Person-Allowed Project Computers

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-473
unit_type: decision
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: |-
  Jared's decisions, verbatim (2026-11-09):
  - Who wins: "Person's pin wins".
  - A build's computers: "Any allowed computer. It should work similar to the way T3 does it where we have a number of parameters to give certain devices priority. Like ram, cpu or storage. We would need to talk through that priority system."
  - Offline mid-task: "Wait, then safe retry".
  - No-project chats: "Keep the computer you're on".
  - Controls: "Presets + Advanced (Recommended)".
  - Measures in Balanced: "Free CPU and memory (Recommended), Free disk space, Queued work (Recommended)".
  - A computer in use: "Yes, count it as Less often (Recommended)".
  - Levels: "As proposed (Recommended)".

  Each Project has a default Computer and new Project work defaults to Auto. SIR-056 owns the single placement policy: must-haves gate before ranking; levels Prefer/Normal/Less often/Only when I choose it; Balanced default, Fastest and Keep my computer free presets; Everywhere weights and optional Project preset override. Tasks add only minimums, never priority. Keyboard activity or battery power demotes to Less often by default, with an off setting. Has the files already was not chosen for Balanced; it exists only as an Advanced slider with default 0. Tie-break is Project default Computer then stable execution_host_id order, unchanged by rename. Why this computer accompanies Auto → <Computer> or Chosen: <Computer> with chooser and requested/effective differences.

  A person's pin binds agents unless the person lets them choose. Agents may pin one task or choose Auto only within allowed Computers; they never change Project/Everywhere defaults. PS-147/148 grants authorize the Project's current person-allowed Computers, including a Computer the person allows later, while each dispatch freezes one exact selection and rechecks authority. A new Computer/device identity still asks even in YOLO. Started work waits/resumes on its Computer; only a safe checkpoint, reconciliation and old-owner fencing permit retry elsewhere. Unstarted independent work may use Auto elsewhere. Home Server remains the records home and never automatically fails over. SRV-017 and general.interaction.no-project-default-computer remain unchanged.

  The must-haves are answering/trusted identity, Project allowance, files or permission to fetch, actual-worker sign-ins/tools, task minimums and not drained. Absolute memory/disk floors in GB, running-task reservations and leased browsers/recordings/phones/exclusive GPU slots remain governor gates. Quota belongs to an account, not a Computer. Related chains, fair caps, measured file latency/health, timing-sensitive versus heavy work, OS-correct memory and durable-runner/restart risk feed existing admission and truthful explanation; none widens authority. Precise scoring calibration and governed grant/context/typed-command successors remain implementation prerequisites, not fabricated native support. Prose precedes inventory/schema/fixture companions; no governance reseal is authorized.
gui_related: true
gui_classification_reason: Defines visible placement choices, controls and explanations.

### DL-476 - One Model Defaults List And Jared Model Answers

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-476
unit_type: decision
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: |-
  Jared answered the model-design questions at about 11:55 PM EST on 2026-11-11, relayed by pm7-build in the settings batch 3 brief. The answers, verbatim as relayed, are:
  MD1: "A".
  MD2: "NEITHER".
  MD3: "A".
  MD4: "A".
  Helper agents, verbatim: "If a helper is a subagent, then the main agent should be able to choose any model it wants at any effort level that is available. There shouldnt be a separate setting for it, if it needs a default, it can follow the other default settings like a regular agent would."
  The which-wins line, verbatim: "What you pick for a run wins; then the account's own default if you sent the run to that account; then this project's list; then Everywhere."
  The accepted design is one list in Settings > Models, with thinking depth chosen inside each model picker. MD1 A permits the same list for This project with Everywhere fallback. MD2 NEITHER removes Persona model/service/preset/effort and command model fields, not merely their priority: old definitions remain compatibility-read only. MD3 A activates an account's own model/depth only when the person sends the run to that account and no earlier source names a model. MD4 A makes Reading pictures the first bridge choice with no separately saved backup; later automatic fallback still requires policy permission and disclosure. The helper model and helper-depth rows are removed; a parent may choose any allowed runnable model/effort within existing parent and policy ceilings, otherwise normal defaults apply.
  Behaviour: keep build-internal scoped owner policy and a page's built-in default as technical detail, remove the old Persona, Computer, last-used and provider-default model sources, and retire configurable resolution policy and stored default variants. Preserve all parent/managed/capability/account/currentness/cost gates and requested/effective receipts. Presets stay picker/key shortcuts. Keep the six jobs including Easy, routine jobs, separate checking from cheap implementation, naming on the smallest available model with Off, explaining with its small-model and no-silent-costly-fallback guard, BSD following Checking finished work, and per-kind picture/video/speech/music models. WL4 = B remains accepted: test an exact typed model name with one small call before saving; a refused or unreachable name is never saved, and acceptance proves no capability.
  Behaviour: retire 18 model-related rows with the compatibility reads in settings_inventory.json; admit Easy, routine jobs, one account model/depth field and three enabled-media model rows. Search, All Settings, transfer, Reset and census derive their active admission from that inventory. Old values remain inspectable, never an extra selection source or new write authority. The PRD Builder, Wizard, building and Scout read the common defaults and allow run overrides; their screen redesign is separate.
  Wording: this one Decision_Log entry records both P17 and E13; it does not reseal governance or claim native runtime proof.

### DL-477 - Lost June Rules: Agents Reliability, Dashboard Summary Widgets And Goal Risk Retirement

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-477
unit_type: decision
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: |-
  On 2026-11-12, at about 10:25 AM EST, Jared ruled on three June rules from pldg-20260616-002-orchestrator-goal-runtime-flow that the closure re-audit found lost. pm7-build relayed the rulings verbatim (1112155957-694d):
  1. Agents-page per-agent reliability metric (atom-0069): "Restore it".
  2. Dashboard summary (atom-0068): "I believe those would be widgets on the dashboards that the user can put on there. Maybe those ones default to on there and the user can remove them."
  3. GoalRun risk classification at run start (atom-0040, its risk element): "Retire it. Also I wasn't aware of any of this. The goal system was simplified about 2 months ago and replaced a lot of what was there... The goal runs on the model the user had chosen, there shouldn't be checks or anything. That's not how other platforms handle it."
  Where each lands. Item 1: Plans/FinalGUISpec.md#F3-395 restores the reliability metrics. The Agents page, which is the Agents panel of F3-452 and F3-477, shows for each agent how many of its recorded operations completed, how many failed, crashed or were aborted, how many were retried, and the share that completed, from the OSI-432 coordination records beside its per-agent economics; nothing recorded shows n/a, and the metrics never route, rank, admit, block or choose a model. Only the reliability metric is restored: atom-0069's capability lanes, active assignments, low-end versus high-end role usage and subagent wave participation are not restored by this decision.
  Item 2: the five June items, active goals, stuck/blocked goals, verification/repair status, certification state and cost/budget warnings, become widgets of the existing board model (DL-186, WS-030). Plans/Widget_System.md#WS-032 adds a Goals source with Active goals and Stuck or blocked goals and a Workflows source with Verification and repair status and Certification state, uses Usage's own widget.alert_thresholds as Cost and budget warnings, and puts all five in the Home board's default set, where the user removes any of them like any other widget; FinalGUISpec Appendix C (C.2, C.4) and F3-395 point to it. Under the current Goal system Goals have no verification, repair or certification, so those two widgets show the status of workflow-owned reviews and certifications (GRS-049, GRS-065), never a Goal's; the Goals widgets read Goal state (GRS-048, GRS-050, GRS-051). Home is the board because it is the default, pinned dashboard where the June rule's project-level summary belongs; Metrics, Monitoring, custom dashboards and Agents are unchanged, and a Home board already saved is not rewritten.
  Item 3: the pre-run classification of a GoalRun's risk by a high-end Goal Controller is retired on purpose, not lost. No risk tier, risk rating, risk register or pre-run classification is restored for Goals: a Goal runs on the model of the chat that started it, with no Goal-owned checks (GRS-049, DL-475), and the closure re-audit's not_supported rows for atom-0040's risk element close as retired by this decision. The atom's GoalRun owner, GRS-026, is retired with the Goal-leftover sweep (DL-478); this decision edits no GRS unit.
  This decision adds no widget model, board, engine, layout key, command or event, does not reseal governance and claims no native implementation.

### DL-479 - One Model Nicknames List For Chat And Media Models

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-479
unit_type: decision
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: |-
  Jared reviewed Settings on 2026-11-13. His review item 4, verbatim: "There is a field that says model nicknames...It makes no sense, it doesnt let you set any values that make sense, this is pointless."
  The stream P lead asked, verbatim: "Model nicknames (your item 4): the specs keep nicknames so you can type a short name like "opus" or "nano banana" instead of a full model name, but Settings shows them as two separate rows both called Model nicknames: a bare text field and a key/value box. What should it become?"
  Jared answered "One nickname list (Recommended)". The option read, verbatim: "One "Model nicknames" list for chat and media models. Each line is a nickname plus the model it means, chosen with the shared model picker. Typing a nickname in chat still works. Replaces both current rows."
  The accepted design is one row, ai.models.model-alias, "Model nicknames", on Settings › Models › Presets and nicknames, for chat and media models. A line is a nickname and the model it means, stored as the canonical provider_id/model_id with no depth; presets, not nicknames, hold a model plus depth (Models_System §6.7). The model is chosen with the shared chat model picker as an overlay under the same rules as a model row: an exact typed name passes one small call before saving. The Models_System §6.8 built-ins are listed in the same list, marked built in; a line whose normalized nickname matches one replaces it for lookup, and removing that line brings the built-in back. The stored value holds only the person's own lines; the default is {}.
  Behaviour: nicknames normalize per §6.7. A second nickname that normalizes the same as one already in the list at that level is refused with the reason, and so is a nickname that equals an exact model id, because it would hide that model. A nickname never proves the model is available (§6.8). Everywhere is home and a project may differ; Computer is not offered (same_for_you) and Device is not offered (not_about_the_screen). Each nickname resolves on its own, expressed with the existing per_item combine keyed by the normalized nickname under SSYS-059: a project's line wins for that nickname, and nicknames set only Everywhere still apply in the project. Typing a nickname in chat still works. A value saved in the row's former shape (one nickname kept inside a model's record) reads as that model's line Everywhere, under the same refusals.
  Behaviour: media.image.model-aliases retires into retired_input_ids and compatibility_reads in settings_inventory.json, replacement ai.models.model-alias, with omit_retired_key, explain_retirement and omit_with_notice. Its read rule merges the person's own entries at the same level (Everywhere or This project), drops an entry only when its normalized nickname and resolved canonical model both equal a shipped built-in pair (the same nickname with another model is the person's override and merges, and an unresolvable model is listed for review), shows a Computer-level entry once for review and never applies it silently, and on a clash keeps the Model nicknames entry and lists the other. The six settings snapshot enums swap media.image.model-aliases for ai.models.model-alias. Search, All Settings, transfer, Reset and census derive their active admission from the inventory.
  Wording: this entry records Jared's batch 4 answer; it does not reseal governance or claim native runtime proof.
gui_related: true
gui_classification_reason: Owns the visible Model nicknames list, its refusals, levels, compatibility disclosure, Settings
  search and transfer behavior.
depends_on:
- SSYS-077
- SSYS-059
- MS-052
- MS-053
unblocks: []
acceptance_criteria:
- Jared's item 4 words, the lead's question, his answer and the option text are preserved verbatim.
- Exactly one active Model nicknames row exists, ai.models.model-alias, Everywhere with optional This project lines, resolved per nickname, default {}.
- media.image.model-aliases is retired with a compatibility read whose replacement is ai.models.model-alias; it gains no new writer.
- The compatibility read drops only an exact built-in pair, so nano banana naming gemini-2.5-flash-image drops as redundant while nano banana naming another model is the person's override and merges.
- A nickname never proves availability; duplicates after normalization and nicknames equal to an exact model id are refused with the reason.
validation_surfaces:

- python3 scripts/pm-plans-verify.py validate-plans-to-code-handoff-schema
- python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_pm_settings_draft_transfer.py

### DL-510: Source Control source records (retention deck 6, E6-1)

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-510
unit_type: decision
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: |-
  Jared answered card E6-1 of retention deck 6 in chat on 2026-11-13 at 10:43 PM EST (03:43Z on 2026-11-14); pm7-build relayed it. His answer, verbatim: "Same as the history". That is option A.

  The question, as the card asked it: "How long should Source Control's saved source records be kept?" Each of the 19 Source Control event types saves a history entry, which already has a keep-rule (DL-453, DL-454 and DL-455), and a separate source record of what actually happened, which the history entry points back to. Option A, "Same lifetime as each history entry", keeps every history entry able to show its source and repeats the rule DL-507 chose for the developer-tool source records.

  That answer keeps each Source Control original source fact exactly as long as the history entry that points to it. The following 19 exact prepared stored values (Plans/source_control_event_storage_rows.json) receive their family's history policy:
  - DL-453 history (kept permanently, no age or count expiry): RP-AUTHORITY-INDEFINITE@1.0.0: source_control_backend_selected_fact (SP-1251), source_control_checkpoint_created_fact (SP-1252), source_control_checkpoint_restored_fact (SP-1253), source_control_repository_bound_fact (SP-1260), source_control_repository_unbound_fact (SP-1261), source_control_workspace_created_fact (SP-1263), source_control_workspace_removed_fact (SP-1265), source_control_writer_lease_granted_fact (SP-1267), source_control_writer_lease_lost_fact (SP-1268).
  - DL-454 history (90 days from the first successful save that survives a restart): RP-TELEMETRY-90D@1.0.0: source_control_backend_detected_fact (SP-1250), source_control_status_refreshed_fact (SP-1262), source_control_workspace_opened_fact (SP-1264), source_control_workspace_switched_fact (SP-1266).
  - DL-455 history (seven years from the original saved change): RP-OPERATIONAL-2555D@1.0.0 under the Storage Project first-save anchor adapter: source_control_remote_fetch_completed_fact (SP-1254), source_control_remote_fetch_started_fact (SP-1255), source_control_remote_publish_completed_fact (SP-1256), source_control_remote_publish_started_fact (SP-1257), source_control_remote_sync_completed_fact (SP-1258), source_control_remote_sync_started_fact (SP-1259).
  All 19 families are Project-only, so no application edition and no application allowance applies.

  For these exact stored values this decision supersedes the earlier PENDING_RETENTION_DECISION statements in SCS-1250 through SCS-1268 (C7), SP-1250 through SP-1268, Plans/source_control_event_preparation.json and Plans/source_control_event_storage_rows.json. Existing policy definitions keep their anchors, counting scopes, counts, overflow actions, stronger holds and required dependencies. Snapshot bodies, native receipts, checkpoint contents, repository files and credential resources keep their independently assigned policies. This assigns no additional family, changes no schema or frozen recipe, and grants no admission, hold release, native execution or governance seal.

### DL-511 - A Supplemental Closure Row May Replace The Frozen Matrix Row It Names

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-511
unit_type: decision
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: >-
  DL-511 records Jared's answer of 2026-11-14 at 3:39 PM EST (20:39:58Z) to stream C's card C-A006: option A,
  "Change the rule so a correction can replace a frozen record", given with no added words. The signed answer is
  /mnt/Cursor/agent-reports/v1/answers/vm.pm-closure-lead--C-A006.json (SHA-256
  ebbc55c2ed72504b9e9d2145ac92855629d9bc7e2a4553f2a594aecc0d493218). The card asked about audit-20260617-006, whose
  frozen closure-matrix lines 22 and 23 still declare the support files scripts/pm-audit-closure.py and
  Plans/.audits/_semantic_closure_registry.jsonl as owners while the registry closures they name were corrected to
  PDS-014 and PLS-012, so neither registry link holds. PLS-026 kept such a link an error, and an appended correction
  changed nothing, because the per-audit check judged every frozen row on its own. Option A promised that the finding
  is properly repaired and closed, that registry rows 25, 35 and 1203 all get final outcomes, and that later audits can
  fix a wrong link the same way. It changes three things. First, Plans/Planning_Ledger_System.md#PLS-026 lets a
  supplemental closure pass append one corrected closure row that names, in replaces_matrix_line, the one frozen row it
  replaces, with replaces_row_sha256 and a replacement_reason; the frozen row stays byte-identical as history, the
  per-audit check judges the replacing row's registry link instead of the frozen row's, and a registry link that does
  not hold stays an error for every frozen row that no valid replacement names. Second, validate_audit_dir in
  scripts/pm-audit-closure.py honors only a valid replacement; it refuses an unknown line, a target that is not a
  frozen row, duplicate and chained replacements, and a replacing row whose own registry link does not hold, and a
  replacing row adds no coverage of its own. Third, audit-20260617-006's supplemental_closure_pass-20261114.json
  replaces lines 22 and 23 with appended rows that link two new registry closures under the corrected owners. They get
  new closure ids, so the existing anchors on closure ids -022 and -023 keep naming exactly one row each. The
  re-audits of registry rows 1203, 25 and 35 follow at the landed commit with fresh reviews; this entry claims no
  re-audit outcome.

### DL-693 - A Restore Point Records Everything Up To Its Message, Sorted By Kind (E10-1)

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-693
unit_type: decision
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: |-
  Jared answered stream E's card E10-1 on the AI Account Center Status tab on 2026-11-15 at 12:51 AM EST (05:51:30Z), signed; pm7-build relayed it in mail 1115055331-5426. His answer: option A, "Everything up to that message, sorted by kind", with no added words.

  The question, as the card asked it: "When you save a restore point in a chat, what should it remember?" A restore point keeps four lists of what the conversation used up to its message (what the user added to the chat's context, the sources behind the answers, files attached to messages and sources the answers cite), and no plan said what goes into each list. Option A promised: "Context: what you added to the chat's context. Sources: what tools and the model used for each answer. Attachments: files on messages. Citations: sources an answer cites. Going back brings back everything the chat had then." Its stated cost: "Larger restore points." Options B, "Only what that one message used", and C, "Only attached files and citations", were not chosen.

  That answer defines how cmd.chat.create_restore_point fills the four frozen capture lists over the inclusive message boundary, in Plans/assistant-chat-design.md#ACD-465 ("Capture selection (DL-693)"). The range is the source conversation branch's persisted transcript up to and including the chosen message. context_refs holds what the user added to the chat's context and still had there at that message; provenance_refs holds, for every answer in the range, the sources its tools and its model used to write it; attachment_refs holds the files attached to messages in the range; citation_refs holds the sources the answers in the range cite. Each list keeps a ref once, in first-appearance order, and the canonical record's context_provenance_refs is context_refs followed by the provenance refs not already in it. Messages after the boundary, other branches, drafts, queued messages and streams add nothing. Every existing rule stays: the frozen categories, their unique union equal to canonical context_provenance_refs, no new redaction transform, the forbidden ephemeral stream and queue data, workspace file bodies, secrets and credentials, and refuse or quarantine for unresolved or unhandled material, which now includes a context item that cannot be placed against the boundary.

  This changes no schema, hash recipe, identity recipe, retention policy, event admission or GUI, and claims no native execution, readiness clearance or governance seal.
gui_related: false
gui_classification_reason: Defines which stored refs a restore point captures; no visible control or layout changes.

- Plans/assistant-chat-design.md#ACD-465 defines each of the four capture lists over the inclusive boundary of the source branch, with first-appearance order and the merged context_provenance_refs order.
- Every existing capture rule is kept; unplaceable, unresolved or forbidden selected material refuses or quarantines and is never dropped or redacted.
- Plans/Automated_Testing_System.md#ATS-3880 executes the selection as real predicates with single-defect witnesses.

### DL-695 - A Retried Failed Deletion Stays Hidden And Re-Checks Before Carrying On (E11-1)

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-695
unit_type: decision
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: |-
  Jared answered stream E's card E11-1 on the AI Account Center Status tab on 2026-11-15 at 11:05 AM EST (16:05:40Z), signed, in send a5dd87b4-e1e1-4992-8c92-1628b73211ad. His answer: option A, "It stays hidden; the retry re-checks and carries on", with no added words.

  The question, as the card asked it: "When a failed deletion is retried, does the content stay hidden?" Storage deletes in steps (hidden from view, held while anything still needs it, permanently purged), and the plans said a retry after a failed step must re-check everything and may not skip straight to purging, but never said which step the retry starts from. Option A promised: "The content never reappears during a retry." Its stated cost: "A retry can't undo the hide; restoring the content goes through the normal restore path." Option B, "It starts over as a new request", was not chosen.

  That answer defines the one edge out of `failed` in the Storage deletion lifecycle, in Plans/storage-plan.md Case L-3 Thread/project deletion (owner unit SP-237): a retried `failed` deletion goes to `logically_hidden`. The retry keeps the same `deletion_id` and deletion-operation idempotency identity, takes the next `event_refs` ordinal (SP-2200), and before it records `logically_hidden` revalidates holds, tombstone, scope, storage-writer posture and purge/compaction authority, proving the content-free tombstone and logical hide again. `held`, `purge_pending` and `purged` then follow only through the ordinary graph. A retry whose revalidation is missing or fails is refused with zero effect and the record stays `failed`. There is no `failed -> requested` edge and no bypass from `failed` to `purge_pending` or `purged`. Every existing rule stays: the failure ingress `requested | logically_hidden | purge_pending -> failed`, the forbidden `held -> failed` and `purged -> failed`, the fail-closed admission order and its zero-effect refusals.

  This changes no payload or record field, identity recipe, deletion window, hold rule, retention policy, event admission or GUI, and claims no native execution, readiness clearance or governance seal.
gui_related: false
gui_classification_reason: Defines the retry successor in the Storage deletion lifecycle; no visible control or layout changes.
depends_on: [DL-045, SP-237, SP-2200]
unblocks: [SP-237, ATS-3920]
acceptance_criteria:
- Plans/storage-plan.md Case L-3 Thread/project deletion states that the graph-valid successor of a revalidated retry is exactly failed -> logically_hidden, with no failed -> requested edge and no bypass to purge_pending or purged.
- Every existing deletion rule is kept; an incomplete or failed retry revalidation refuses with zero effect and leaves the record failed.
- Plans/Automated_Testing_System.md#ATS-3920 executes the retry edge as real predicates with single-defect witnesses and refusals for retries to requested, purge_pending and purged and for missing revalidation.
